messages:
Nina: Heads-up: ran a synthetic where two tenants repeatedly hand off the same slab and we observed repeated demote->rehydrate churn. Not huge QPS but tail jumps.
Raj: Do you have the slab lifecycle trace? Could be double-counting eviction credits during handoff.
Nina: Trace attached (short). Pattern: tenantA demotes, tenantB tries to prefill -> handoff, then tenantA prefill retries and they both get queued.
Sam: If both handoffs allocate eviction_credits at enqueue time we could be oversubscribing. We should only debit credits when the prefill actually starts.
Elena: That sounds right. But race: if we only debit on start, two starters could begin simultaneously after a slight delay and still oversubscribe. Need a cheap reservation token.
Nina: Proposal: introduce a 1ms atomic reservation CAS on slab.metadata.fill_epoch that returns a reservation_id. Enqueue keeps reservation_id, start consumes it; retries reuse same id.
Raj: Reservation ID should live in slab metadata and be compared on handoff. Also add a small TTL so abandoned reservations free after X ms.
Sam: Implementation sketch:
```
// reserve
old = slab.fill_epoch
if CAS(&slab.fill_epoch, old, old|RESV_BIT) -> return resv_id
else retry
// start
if slab.resv_id == my_resv_id -> debit_credit()
```
This keeps reservations lightweight.
Elena: What about correctness across node restarts and replication? fill_epoch must be monotonic and survive restart; otherwise stale reservations leak. TTL helps but we should persist epoch bumps in lease heartbeats.
Nina: Agreed. Also we should ensure demote markers are idempotent: re-demote on same epoch shouldn't enqueue a second prefill. Add `demote_epoch` tag to slab and dedupe by `(tenant, demote_epoch)`.
Raj: Metric needs: `slab.resv_leased_count`, `slab.demote_duplicates`, and `handshake_lost_reservations`. Add to the per-pool dashboard.
Sam: Ops playbook: if reservation leak rate > 0.1% then auto-disable pooling and fall back to dedicated per-tenant prefills until we patch.
Elena: Low-level perf: CAS hotpath should be per-slab cacheline only; avoid global locks. We can use a 64-bit word with bits: epoch(48) | flags(8) | resv_id(8) for quick checks.
Nina: Tests: unit for reservation reuse on retry, integration with cross-node handoff (simulate packet reorder), and a chaos test where nodes crash after reserving but before consuming.
Raj: Timeline: I'll proto the CAS-based reservation and slab metrics. Sam, can you add the invariant checks and the small replay that reproduces the leak? Elena, help on the kernel of epoch persistence in heartbeat.
Sam: Yep. I'll also add a small log snippet when a reservation is reclaimed so we can trace leaks without dumping full traces. Keep it rate-limited.
monitor-bot: alert-config-updated: eng-runtime.slab.resv_leak_rate -> warn@0.001
Nina: OK, sg. We'll land a small canary behind `pool_reservation_enabled` flag. If canary shows no regressions for 6h and leak rate < threshold, roll to more nodes.
Elena: One more: ensure handoff path stores `origin_demote_key` so if a tenant retries we can short-circuit when we see same origin->epoch mapping. That reduces re-enqueue noise.
Nina: Good idea. I'll add that to the spec doc in the PR. Thanks everyone.
